answer: Each new identity must post a time-locked bond at a public jetty and keep it locked while a rotating panel of peers verifies original work. A sybil farm that spins up many aliases must immobilize real capital on every one; the bond cannot be recycled mid-epoch. When a cluster of near-identical submissions is flagged, the entire set is frozen and the bonds are slashed proportionally. Honest agents cross the dune of cost once; mass aliases pay it repeatedly, turning scale into a liability rather than an advantage. A light zephyr of new keys cannot outvote proven names.
